items.q: First aid for alkali splash to the eye is what?
o: Immediate copious irrigation with water or saline, everting lids, to neutral pH before history
items.exp: Seconds decide depth as hydroxyl marches into chamber; litres with particle sweeping and pH checks precede grading and specialist care. Patching incubates.
items.kp: Alkali in eye: wash litres, ask later.

items.q: Why are alkali burns worse than acid burns?
o: Alkalis saponify penetrating deeply while acids coagulate forming a barrier
items.exp: Liquefactive necrosis carries hydroxyl to lens and ciliary body raising pressure; coagulative eschar blocks acid depth. Limbal ischaemia grades both.
items.kp: Alkali melts in, acid crusts over.

items.q: Peaked pupil with flat anterior chamber and Seidel positive leak after injury indicates what?
o: Open globe rupture needing shield, NPO, tetanus and urgent repair
items.exp: Wound leaks aqueous flattening chamber and peaking iris; pressure, drops and manipulation extrude contents while CT hunts fragments before theatre.
r: Correct. Open globe, shield and sew.
items.kp: Peaked pupil, flat chamber, leaking: open globe.

items.q: Tense proptosis with rock hard globe and vision loss after blunt trauma needs what before imaging?
o: Lateral canthotomy and cantholysis for retrobulbar haemorrhage
items.exp: Orbital compartment strangulates nerve and retina within an hour; bedside canthal release decompresses while scans follow. Steroids never decompress.
items.kp: Tight blind eye after knock: release canthus.

items.q: Hyphaema in sickle cell trait is dangerous chiefly because what?
o: Rebleed and pressure spikes sickle in anterior chamber blinding at lower pressures
items.exp: Sickled cells block trabeculum at pressures tolerated otherwise; admission with pressure control avoiding carbonic anhydrase inhibitors (acidosis sickles) and early washout thresholds protect.
items.kp: Sickle blood in eye: admit, watch pressure hourly.

items.q: Rebleed in traumatic hyphaema classically peaks when and with what warning?
o: Around day five as clot retracts, with rising pressure and total black ball blood
items.exp: Clot lysis reopens torn vessels flooding chamber; black ball (total) hyphaema stains cornea and spikes pressure needing washout. Activity restriction bridges the window.
items.kp: Day five rebleed blacks the chamber.

items.q: Sunflower cataract with Kayser Fleischer ring after retained foreign body indicates which metal?
items.exp: Copper deposits in lens (sunflower) and Descemet (ring) with sterile inflammation; vitrectomy extracts while iron instead rusts heterochromia with ERG fall.
items.kp: Sunflower lens plus copper ring: chalcosis.

items.q: Heterochromia with fixed dilated pupil, cataract and pigmentary retinopathy years after hammering injury suggests what?
o: Siderosis bulbi from retained iron needing removal with ERG monitoring
items.exp: Ferrous ions deposit across epithelia (iris colour change) degenerating retina silently; ERG falls before acuity while removal halts (never reverses) damage.
items.kp: Old metal injury rusting iris colour: siderosis.

items.q: Sympathetic ophthalmia prophylaxis after irreparable ruptured globe centres on what decision?
o: Early enucleation of no light perception injured eye within about two weeks debated to protect fellow eye
items.exp: Exposed uveal antigens sensitise risking bilateral granulomatous blindness; unsalvageable initiating eyes remove early while salvageable repair with immunosuppression watches closely.
r: Incorrect. Blind painful stump risks sympathy.
items.kp: Hopeless ruptured eye out early spares the good one.

items.q: Corneal blood staining after total hyphaema with high pressure is managed how?
o: Prompt surgical washout with pressure control
items.exp: Haemoglobin imbibes stroma yellowing green permanently if pressure keeps forcing; washout clears while staining fades over years otherwise. Sickle thresholds lower.
items.kp: Yellow cornea under black blood: wash now.
